title: Tuple chains and explicit ordered-coset comparison maps
statement: For a set Y and integer q, a tuple symbol is a list in Y of length q+1 and B_q(Y) is its free integer module on the specified Finsupp basis [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. A list of the wrong length denotes zero. The tuple boundary is alternating positional deletion and a map of sets acts coordinatewise. For a group G, subgroup H, n in N and a:Fin(n+1)→G, let X_i be the separately labeled subtype of elements ha_i, h∈H. Chosen vertices are ha_i and translation by g∈H sends x to gx. Use the colored-face chain groups and operators of [def-sfb-ordered-join-chains]. Arity k has degree k-1, including -1 when k=0. The recursive map P is identity on the empty generator at arity zero, sends h to the color-zero vertex ha_0 at arity one, and at higher arities applies the contraction based at the first entry to P of the alternating boundary. Erasure e lists vertices by increasing color. Define A=eP. These are the actual finite formulas extracted unchanged from [lem-sfb-ordered-join-coset-comparison], not arbitrary witnesses of an existence theorem.
